items.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002
items.q: Billy Drummond, a lot of the young musicians would just go up and play all the time.

ctx.x: Let’s see, well the late 1980s we’re talking like the Blue Note had a late night jam session, like after the last show during the week and so usually starting at 1:00. And people like Justin Robertson and the Harper Brothers were heading those jam sessions. Then there was a jam session uptown at this place called Augie’s, which is now called Smoke. But Augie’s was a place where a lot of guys honed their craft, guys like Larry Goldings and Freddy Bryant, a young guitarist I’ve been working with for quite a while,
Billy Drummond, a lot of the young musicians would just go up and play all the time. The Village — not the Village Vanguard but the other club—
